newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank says intervened less in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank says intervened less in latest week.

text.p: The flow of funds into markka decreased in the week to January 23 compared to the previous week, easing pressure on the central bank to intervene, a Bank of Finland official said on Monday.

"Our impression was that in the balance sheet week (to January 23) there was less inflow of funds compared to the previous week," head of market operations Olli-Pekka Lehmussaari told Reuters by telephone.
"Thus the number of interventions decreased," he added.
Lehmussaari said that when the Finnish markka strengthened beyond 2.90 against the mark last Monday, "it proved that the central bank has not sought to keep a tight currency fluctuation band".
The Bank of Finland said its foreign currency reserves rose 11.5 billion markka in the week to January 23, compared with a 15.7 billion markka increase in the previous balance sheet week.
Market operators said the increase in foreign currency reserves was roughly in line with their expectations.
With the markka's sharp strengthening trend over for now, it was unlikely the Bank of Finland would continue to increase its reserves at this pace, operators said.
Bank of Finland director Matti Vanhala said last Monday the central bank had adopted a more liberal approach in foreign exchange intervention than in the previous week.
